violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squeeze bottles of different types of dressings.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC labeled all squeeze bottles of different types of dressings during inspection.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PIC placed wiping cloths in sanitizer solution.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed spatulas in the water container at 84F next to induction stove.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC removed spatulas from water container, then rinsed and sanitized them properly.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: PIC Duties, No Unnecessary Persons
violations.observation: Observed several office workers walk through the kitchen to access an internal stairwell.
violations.corrective_action: Persons unnecessary to the food establishment operation are not allowed in the food preparation, food storage, or ware washing areas of the commercial establishment. Only approved tours or brief visits may be authorized by the Person in Charge or certified food manager if steps are taken to ensure that exposed food, clean equipment/utensils, clean linens, and single service items are protected from contamination. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ONLY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT EMPLOYEES ARE AUTHORIZED TO BE IN THE KITCHEN. CORRECT THIS VIOLATION. PIC STATES HE WILL DISCUSS WITH TOPIC WITH THE BUILDING MANAGEMENT.

out_items.name: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated

violations.title: Safe, Unadulterated & Honestly Presented
violations.observation: Observed moldy heavy cream and pickled jalapeños in the walk-in cooler
violations.corrective_action: ALL food shall be safe, unadulterated and honestly presented as specified under 3-601.12. PIC DISCARDED THE FOOD.

out_items.name: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding

violations.title: Reheating for Hot Holding, Commercially Processed Food
violations.observation: Observed commercially processed sausage patties being reheated in the countertop steam well. Sausage patties were observed at 22-90f. Upon discussion with staff, frozen patties were placed in the steam well to reheat.
violations.corrective_action: Ready-to-eat food taken from a commercially processed, hermetically sealed container or from an intact package from a food processing plant shall be reheated for hot holding to a minimum temperature of 135F to be maintained in hot hold at 135F or above. PIC REHEATED THE SAUSAGE PATTIES IN THE CONVEYOR OVEN UNTIL THE TEMPERATURE REACHED 168f.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) sliced chicken shawarma was observed at 130f in the countertop steam well; 2) roasted potatoes were observed at 80f at ambient temperature. Upon discussion with PIC, potatoes were cooked 2 hours prior to inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC REHEATED THE CHICKEN IN THE CONVEYOR OVEN UNTIL THE TEMPERATURE WAS 176f. PIC WILL DISCARD THE POTATOES IN 2 HOURS. THE COMMONS FOODERIE (Inspection Date: 02/10/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) commercial garlic toum was observed at 66f at ambient temperature. Upon discussion with PIC, garlic toum was taken out of the cooler 2 hours prior to inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC AGREED TO DISCARD GARLIC TOUM IN 2 HOURS.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: Observed inconsistent date marking throughout the facility. Observed no date marking on the prepared mango lassi, yogurt parfaits, and cut fruit cups.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC TO DATE MARK ALL FOODS THAT ARE TO BE STORED FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS. PIC INSTRUCTED STAFF TO START DATE MARKING THE AFOREMENTIONED FOODS. SEE DATE MARKING HAND OUT. THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: sunflower seeds, chia seeds, maple syrup, caramel sauce, etc.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. LABEL ALL FOOD STORAGE CONTAINERS.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Two employees were observed without a hair restraint.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. ALL STAFF MUST WEAR A HAIR RESTRAINT (ie: HAT, HAIRNET, ETC.)

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.observation: Observed clean utensils and mugs being stored under paper towel dispenser and soap dispenser. Clean items are subjected to splashing and dripping from water and soap as employees use the hand washing sinks.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC TO MOVE THE PAPER TOWEL DISPENSERS AND SOAP DISPENSER TO A DIFFERENT LOCATION THAT DOES NOT SUBJECT CLEAN EQUIPMENT TO POTENTIAL CONTAMINATION.
